definitions.explanation: A person who does not appreciate or acknowledge kindness received. Also used as an adjective to describe such behavior.

examples.japanese: {恩知|おんし}らずな⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧だ。
⟦あれ→あれ：00916_are⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦{助|たす}けて→助ける：00895_tasukeru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、{恩知|おんし}らず⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧ほど⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: After receiving so much help, there's a limit to how ungrateful you can be.

examples.japanese: {恩知|おんし}らず⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われたくなかった→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦お{礼|れい}→お礼：01359_orei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: I didn't want to be called ungrateful, so I wrote a thank-you letter.

notes:
FORMS:
⟦{恩|おん}→恩：02550_on⟧ (kindness, favor, debt of gratitude) + ⟦{知|し}ら→知る：00458_shiru⟧ず (not knowing). Literally "not knowing kindness."

USAGE:
A strong word of criticism. Used as a na-adjective ({恩知|おんし}らずな) or as a noun to refer to an ungrateful person. Carries significant moral weight in Japanese culture, where gratitude (⟦{恩|おん}→恩：02550_on⟧) and repaying kindness (⟦{恩返|おんがえ}し→恩返し：11063_ongaeshi⟧) are deeply valued.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {恩知|おんし}らずな⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (an ungrateful person)
- {恩知|おんし}らずな⟦{態度|たいど}→態度：03396_taido⟧ (ungrateful attitude)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{恩返|おんがえ}し→恩返し：11063_ongaeshi⟧ (repaying a debt of gratitude)
- ⟦{恩|おん}に{着|き}る→恩に着る：19331_onnikiru⟧ (to feel indebted)
